thread:
Ben: Heads-up — saw a regression in prefix cache hit-rate after last night's kernel-selector tweak. p50 fine, but short-prompt p95/p99 jumped.
Ana: ugh, when did that land? commit/sha?
Ben: rolled at 03:12 UTC, sha `a7f3d9b`. Kernel selector now prefers the new fused-attn kernel for sequence lengths <= 64.
Vikram: that should be good normally. do we have profiling showing why cache hit-rate dropped?
Ben: yes — quick summary from a 30m sample on prod:
- prior cache.hitrate (short prompts): 83%
- after change: 57%
- p99 token-latency (short): 48ms -> 122ms
- observed a spike in KV scan time for cache misses: +3.1x
Sasha: interesting. could be cache-key canonicalization or client-side header handshake mismatch. any evidence?
Ben: grep of traces shows a large number of requests missing the `X-RW-PFX-KEY` header when routed to the new kernel pool. The runtime path that serializes canonical keys (the canonicalizer) wasn't wired into the fast-path.
Ana: so kernel selector route bypassed canonicalization -> different cache keys -> lower hit rate. makes sense.
Vikram: what's the impact of retries/streaming here? I recall some clients retry on slow streams which could cause duplicate warmup traffic.
Ben: yes — we saw an uptick in 429/retry loops for streaming edges. SDKs were retrying without preserving `X-RW-Cache-Opt` header (opt-in), so retries effectively re-probed the cache and evicted some prefix entries via TTL churn.
Sasha: we need three actions: 1) patch canonicalizer into fast-path, 2) add server-side guard to normalize keys before lookup, 3) SDK change to preserve cache opt header on retries.
Ana: + telemetry change: emit `cache.lookup_normalized` boolean and `cache.key_entropy` histogram so we can see mismatches.
Vikram: also propose a controlled warmup: sample-based prefill for the new kernel pool, e.g., 1% of traffic serve a warmup probe that touches likely prefixes rather than full live retries. That avoids churn.
Ben: agree. sample-warmup plan:
```
- when rolling new kernel:
  - mark new pool as `prefill: true`
  - start 1% sampled probes that include headers: `X-RW-Cache-Opt: opt-in`, `X-RW-Prefill: probe`
  - probes use sequence-length-aware batching (max_batch=8 for <=64 tokens)
```
Sasha: for SDK patch, sample code (JS):
```
// preserve cache opt header across retries
const headers = { 'X-RW-Cache-Opt': client.cacheOpt ? 'opt-in' : 'opt-out' };
await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body });
// ensure retry wrapper copies headers on retry
```
Ana: ops runbook updates: rollback criteria = cache.hitrate for short-prompts < 70% for > 15m OR p99 increase > 2x. Owner: Ben + Vikram. ETA for patch?
Ben: I'll open PR for canonicalizer and server guard today, targed patch by EOD. SDK PR by Sasha tomorrow.
charlie-bot: deploy-bot: started canary deploy to 3 hosts (pool: kernel-v2-fastpath) at 2029-10-06T04:20Z
Vikram: once canary is up, run the warmup-sampler for 30m and validate `cache.hitrate` and `cache.lookup_normalized` metrics. if metrics pass, ramp to 25% then full.
Sasha: one more edge: streaming responses where first chunk triggers prefill but subsequent chunks drop header — we need runtime to snapshot headers at request start and use for all streamed writes.
Ben: noted. add runtime change to carry header-map across stream lifecycle.
Ana: thanks — this actually explains a lot of weird customer reports earlier today. keep updates here.
Sasha: will post PR links when ready :thumbsup:
Ben: thanks team, ping me with any samples or logs (trace ids) you want me to look at.
